definition: Processing capacity used to train models and serve inference. Racks and datacenter tiers add capacity; training jobs and deployed traffic consume it.
Accumulated unaddressed risk. Rises from shipping fast and skipping reviews; falls from safety research, evaluations, and cautious choices.
How much the public and press currently trust the company. Moves from incidents, communications, and ambient public mood.
How closely the regulator is watching. Crossing its threshold triggers an audit with real requirements.
Abstract legal risk. Crossing a case type's threshold files an actual case that must be settled, fought, or left to run its course.
How much of a deployment's potential traffic is actually let through. Keeping it low for too long can permanently churn away users.
A subscription plan's hard seat cap. Demand above it is turned away, not discounted.
Compute permanently set aside for one deployment, guaranteeing it headroom regardless of what else is running.
A capability granted to a deployed model — coding, support, research assistance, tool access, or spending authority. Each is a productivity gain traded for an explicit risk.
How much of the company's work autonomy permissions are doing. Scales the effects of whichever workforce policy is active.
How far a deployment has staged into its current mode (Internal/Beta/Public). Resets to 0% whenever you promote to a new mode.
A model's true, initially hidden risk level. Evaluations narrow the visible range without ever fully revealing it up front.
Background cycles (energy price, chip supply, talent market, public mood, regulation climate) that rise and fall over time and affect the company, independent of anything you do.
One of 5 narrative chapters, unlocked by capability/scale milestones — never a fixed day. See the top bar for your current act.
The founders' share of the company. Drops permanently whenever a funding round's equity is accepted.
How many days of cash remain at the current burn rate, shown in the Company panel's daily ledger.
